Hierarchical kNN Classification

cytoGateR authors

Source: vignettes/Hierarchical_KNN.qmd

1 Overview

Flat classifiers predict among all cell types in a single step. Hierarchical k-nearest-neighbour (kNN) classification instead organizes reference cell types into a tree and predicts one branch at a time. Each internal node separates the cell types on its left branch from those on its right branch. A cell moves recursively through the hierarchy until it reaches a terminal cell type or fails the confidence and agreement requirements.

This vignette demonstrates the complete hierarchical kNN workflow on one complete image from cytoGateR_example.

library(cytoGateR)
data("cytoGateR_example", package = "cytoGateR")

image_ids <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(cytoGateR_example)$image_name
spe <- cytoGateR_example[, image_ids == image_ids[1L]]
spe

2 Prepare reference labels

The packaged core_group column contains high-confidence labels produced by tree gating. Cells outside the high-confidence reference are marked "Unassigned". The hierarchy builders use "Unknown" for cells that should not contribute to the reference, so the labels are harmonized before fitting.

cd <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(spe)
cd$hier_reference_label <- as.character(cd$core_group)
cd$hier_reference_label[cd$hier_reference_label == "Unassigned"] <- "Unknown"
SummarizedExperiment::colData(spe) <- cd

table(SummarizedExperiment::colData(spe)$hier_reference_label)

      Bcell     BnTcell         CD4         CD8     Myeloid  Neutrophil
        236         337         227         206         108          12
Plasma_cell      Stroma        Treg       Tumor     Unknown
         40          71         125          16        2985

3 Build the lineage hierarchy

build_lineage_hierarchy() calculates the average marker-expression profile for each reference cell type and hierarchically clusters those profiles.

hc_tree <- build_lineage_hierarchy(
  spe,
  label_col = "hier_reference_label",
  assay_name = "exprs"
)

hc_tree$labels
 [1] "BnTcell"     "CD4"         "Bcell"       "Treg"        "Plasma_cell"
 [6] "Myeloid"     "CD8"         "Stroma"      "Tumor"       "Neutrophil" 
plot(hc_tree, main = "Hierarchy of reference cell types")

4 Build node-specific references

Each internal node receives its own binary training reference. Labels are converted to "Left" and "Right" according to the branches of hc_tree.

Setting top_n = NULL uses all available markers at each node. For larger panels, marker_stats and top_n can be supplied to retain only the most informative markers for each split.

hier_reference <- build_hierarchical_reference(
  spe,
  hc_tree,
  label_col = "hier_reference_label",
  top_n = NULL,
  assay_name = "exprs",
  unknown_label = "Unknown"
)

names(hier_reference)
[1] "Node_1" "Node_2" "Node_3" "Node_4" "Node_5" "Node_6" "Node_7" "Node_8"
[9] "Node_9"

Inspect the root-node reference:

root_name <- paste0("Node_", nrow(hc_tree$merge))
root_reference <- hier_reference[[root_name]]

dim(root_reference$train_data)
[1] 1378   40
table(root_reference$train_labels)

 Left Right
   16  1362 
root_reference$left_members
[1] "Tumor"
root_reference$right_members
[1] "Bcell"       "CD4"         "Treg"        "BnTcell"     "CD8"
[6] "Plasma_cell" "Stroma"      "Myeloid"     "Neutrophil"

5 Run recursive hierarchical kNN

At each node, predict_hierarchical_knn_recursive() creates an ensemble of weighted kNN predictions. A prediction is accepted only when both its average probability and ensemble agreement pass their thresholds.

The vignette uses one distance method and one repeat for speed. Production analyses can use multiple distance methods and additional repeats for a more stable ensemble.

set.seed(1)
spe <- predict_hierarchical_knn_recursive(
  spe,
  hier_reference,
  hc_tree,
  assay_name = "exprs",
  threshold = 0.5,
  agreement_threshold = 0.5,
  k = 3,
  repeats = 1,
  dist_methods = "pearson",
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam(),
  out_col = "hier_label",
  chunk_size = 1000,
  unassigned_label = "Unassigned"
)

Finally, display the hierarchical predictions in spatial coordinates:

plot_labelled_cells(
  spe,
  col_label = "hier_label",
  image_col = "image_name"
)

7 Production settings

A larger ensemble can combine correlation- and angle-based similarity measures:

spe <- predict_hierarchical_knn_recursive(
  spe,
  hier_reference,
  hc_tree,
  threshold = 0.7,
  agreement_threshold = 0.8,
  k = 5,
  repeats = 5,
  dist_methods = c("pearson", "cosine"),
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)
